question.question: When a replica receives PreAccept for instance (Replica, Instance) while its local record for that instance already has Status >= ACCEPTED but stores no commands, handlePreAccept writes the received command into InstanceSpace[preAccept.LeaderId][Instance] instead of the addressed instance InstanceSpace[preAccept.Replica][Instance]. Is any legal history able to put a replica in that state with preAccept.LeaderId != preAccept.Replica, and if so does the addressed record (Replica, Instance) stay without commands (halting its row's execution and the recovery replies about it) while an unrelated record (LeaderId, Instance) acquires a command that no quorum committed for it?
question.importance: Wrong-slot attribution of a command mutates protocol state without any quorum behind it: a record that never committed that command can become executable as though it had, while the record the message was addressed to can be left permanently unexecutable because executeCommands requires Cmds != nil and findSCC returns false for a command-less instance. Both effects are consensus-visible (an uncommitted command can reach the state machine, and a committed instance can stop making progress).

question.trigger_rationale: Source reading showed the discrepancy directly: S9-handlePreAccept uses preAccept.Replica at lines 782, 792-798, 810, 816 and 828-829, but preAccept.LeaderId at line 809 for the same object. The state needed to reach the branch (Status >= ACCEPTED with nil Cmds on a replica receiving a PreAccept) is not produced by any path read: handleAccept stores bal/vbal/Seq/Deps without recording ACCEPTED (S11-handleAccept), the leader-side ACCEPTED/COMMITTED transitions set Cmds from lb.cmds (S10-handlePreAcceptReply, S12-handleAcceptReply, S18-handleTryPreAcceptReply), handleCommit installs commit.Command (S13-handleCommit), and a marshalled nil command slice comes back as a non-nil empty slice. The reachability premise is therefore resolved as not produced, and the separated remaining premise is whether the accept phase is required to record ACCEPTED.

feedback.answered: The Candidate's discriminator is resolved on sources: no legal history in the captured snapshot establishes the branch premise. A replica that receives PreAccept can hold Status >= ACCEPTED with Cmds == nil only if some local transition sets ACCEPTED, COMMITTED or EXECUTED without also installing commands. handleAccept stores bal, vbal, Seq and Deps but never writes Status, so an acceptor that never saw the PreAccept keeps Status NONE even though it holds accepted attributes (S11-handleAccept). Every transition that does set Status >= ACCEPTED also sets Cmds in the same handler: handlePreAccept stores the received command when it sets PREACCEPTED/PREACCEPTED_EQ (S9-handlePreAccept), the leader-side accept and commit paths set inst.Cmds from lb.cmds (S10-handlePreAcceptReply, S12-handleAcceptReply, S18-handleTryPreAcceptReply), and handleCommit copies commit.Command (S13-handleCommit). A commit command cannot arrive as nil through the wire format: Marshal writes a zero-length prefix and Unmarshal allocates a non-nil empty slice. The only nil-Cmds records are fresh default records with Status NONE (S11-handleAccept, S13-handleCommit, S14-recovery-start-prepare). The line 809 branch is therefore dead code while acceptors do not record acceptance, and the wrong-slot write cannot be reached; the two sourced discrepancies (the LeaderId index and the omitted ACCEPTED status) currently compensate instead of composing into a defect.
remaining: whether the accept phase is required to record ACCEPTED on an acceptor, so that handlePreAccept's >= ACCEPTED guard (S9-handlePreAccept), findPreAcceptConflicts' already-ACCEPTED shortcut (S17-find-conflicts) and handlePrepareReply's sub-case 2 (S15-handlePrepareReply) can observe accept-phase state on a replica that never led the instance
whether the intended acceptor status semantics are external to this snapshot (the corrected EPaxos specification or reference implementation) rather than inferable from in-repository callers
feedback.rationale: The branch premise was the Candidate's open question; enumerating every writer of Instance.Cmds and Instance.Status in the snapshot answers it without execution, so the proposition is explained by the existing (if accidental) protection rather than confirmed as a violated obligation. The consequence chain that would follow if the branch were reachable (wrong-slot command attribution, addressed row left without commands, execution requiring Cmds != nil) stays recorded in the question, but it is not an observed behavior. The separately grounded accept-status premise is a different responsibility and is retained for its own question instead of being folded into this one.
